chapters.summary: Council staff welcomes attendees to the Committee on Governmental Operations, State and Federal Legislation vote, asks everyone to silence electronic devices, and confirms the committee is ready to begin.
chapters.title: Staff opens hearing and gives housekeeping instructions

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to today's New York City Council vote for the Committee on Governmental Operations, State and Federal Legislation.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: At this time, please silence all electronic devices and no one may approach the dais at any time.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair Brewer, we are ready to begin.

chapters.summary: Gale Brewer introduces herself as committee chair and welcomes council members in attendance, including Morano, Wilson, Zhuang, Feliz, Dinowitz, and Carr, noting Carr's Staten Island connection.
chapters.title: Chair Brewer opens hearing and welcomes council colleagues

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I am Gail Brewer, Chair of the Committee on Government Operations, State and Federal Legislation.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you for joining us today.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I would like to welcome my council colleagues who are here, Councilmember Morano, Wilson, Zhuang, Felice, Dinowitz, and Carr.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Carr's here because he's from Staten Island.

chapters.summary: Brewer announces the committee will vote on Council Member Morano's bill, Intro 320A, which would codify the official flag of Staten Island, allowing it to be used at official events.
chapters.title: Brewer introduces Intro 320A to codify the Staten Island borough flag

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Today we will be voting on Councilmember Morano's bill, Intro 320A, which would codify the official flag of Staten Island.

chapters.summary: Brewer explains that currently only Brooklyn and the Bronx have codified their borough flags, joking about Manhattan's absence, and notes the Staten Island flag has been in use since 2016.
chapters.title: Brewer notes only Brooklyn and the Bronx have codified borough flags

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Currently only Brooklyn and the Bronx have codified their flags.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I don't know what's wrong with Manhattan.

chapters.summary: Brewer explains the flag was commissioned by then-Borough President James Otto and replaced a previous flag that was roundly disliked by Staten Island residents. The bill simply codifies the flag already in use.
chapters.title: Brewer describes the flag's history and origins under Borough President James Otto

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: The flag that will be codified.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I have an idea.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: The flag that will be codified by Councilmember Morano's bill has been in use since 2016, replacing a flag that was roundly disliked by Staten Island residents.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I think Jimmy Otto has something to do with this.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: This bill simply codifies a flag that the borough already uses.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Which will allow it to be used at official events.

chapters.summary: Brewer acknowledges Johari Frazier, Erica Cohen, and Senator Hamid from the Government Operations committee, as well as Cynthia Honig and James Liu from her office, noting Liu is from Staten Island.
chapters.title: Brewer thanks committee staff and her office team

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'd like to thank the following people from government operations.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Relations Committee, Johari Frazier, Erica Cohen, and Senator Hamid.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: And from my office, Cynthia Honig and James Liu, who's here today.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: He's from Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Everyone working in the background to make this hearing run smoothly is much appreciated.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I will now turn it over to Councilmember Morano to give a statement on the bill.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I think we also have Councilmember Stevens on Zoom.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'll now turn it over again to Councilmember Morano, who's from Staten Island and loves this flag.

chapters.summary: Frank Morano begins his statement, saying Staten Islanders have never needed a law to be proud of their borough but that their flag should finally have the law on its side. He notes the flag was commissioned by Borough President James Otto and designed by Amal Micah.
chapters.title: Morano: Staten Islanders proud of borough, flag deserves legal recognition

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Thank you to all my colleagues on the Government Operations Committee for considering Intro 320 today.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Staten Islanders, as all of the Staten Island City Council delegation will tell you, has never needed a law to tell us to be proud of our borough.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But after today, hopefully our flag will finally have the law on its side.

chapters.summary: Morano details the flag's imagery: a woman representing New York City standing on Staten Island looking over the Narrows, Henry Hudson's Half Moon, Native Americans and Dutch settlers, symbols of peace, and the dates 1609 and 1898. He calls it 'a history lesson you can raise on a flagpole.'
chapters.title: Morano describes the flag's design and historical symbolism

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: For nearly a decade, as the chair indicated, Staten Islanders have embraced this flag.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It was commissioned by then-Borough President James Otto and designed by Amal Micah and his team to give our borough a symbol worthy of its history.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And there's a lot of history on this flag.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: There's a woman on the flag, you'll see, who represents New York City.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: She's standing on Staten Island and looking out over the Narrows.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: We see Henry Hudson's half moon, Native Americans and Dutch settlers, symbols of peace, and the dates 1609 and 1898.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: In other words, this isn't just a nice design.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's a history lesson you can raise on a flagpole.

chapters.summary: Morano addresses critics who question the bill's importance, arguing that Staten Islanders sometimes feel removed from the rest of the city. He says the more connected New Yorkers feel to their borough, the more connected they feel to the city as a whole.
chapters.title: Morano: borough pride and city pride complement each other

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But despite all that, our flag has never actually been official under New York City law.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: As the chair indicated, only the Bronx and Brooklyn currently have their borough flags codified.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So Intro 320 changes that for Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I think there's a larger message here because so many people have asked me, oh, isn't there something more important that you should be worried about?

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And the truth is Staten Islanders sometimes feel a little removed from the rest of New York City, both geographically and otherwise.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Sometimes we're happy to be a little farther removed.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: But borough pride and city pride aren't competitors.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I believe the more connected New Yorkers feel to their neighborhood and their boroughs, the more connected they feel to the city as a whole.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's not about putting Staten Island above any other borough.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: It's about putting Staten Island alongside them.

chapters.summary: Morano highlights the nonpartisan support from the entire Staten Island delegation, thanking Majority Whip Hanks and Minority Leader Carr as partners. He notes Staten Island pride brings Democrats and Republicans together and thanks Carr and Camilla for making it a true delegation effort.
chapters.title: Morano thanks bipartisan Staten Island delegation for unified support

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'm particularly proud that our entire Staten Island delegation came together on this in a nonpartisan fashion.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Majority Whip Hanks, Minority Leader Carr, and I may represent different districts and sometimes different points of view, but we share a tremendous love for the borough, and we're privileged to represent it, and that's why we're all on this bill.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I especially want to thank my brother, Minority Leader Carr.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: David has been a friend, a colleague, and a partner on this effort from the beginning.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: There aren't many things in this building that bring Democrats and Republicans together quite as easily as Staten Island pride, and I'm grateful to both David and Camilla for making this a true delegation effort.

chapters.summary: Morano expresses gratitude to Speaker Menin and Chair Brewer for their support, thanks colleagues outside Staten Island who joined the bill, and says he looks forward to the day the flag is raised as the official flag of Staten Island. He urges a yes vote.
chapters.title: Morano thanks Speaker Menin, Chair Brewer, and looks forward to flag-raising

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: I'm also grateful to Speaker Menon and Chair Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: for their support for this entire process, and from my colleagues outside Staten Island who joined us, and everyone who recognizes that these symbols of civic identity really do matter.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So today, we're taking something Staten Islanders have already embraced and simply saying officially and permanently, this is our flag.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I look forward to the day when Kamilla, David, and I can stand together as this flag is raised for the first time as the official flag of the borough of Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: So I hope everybody votes yes.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: And I'm grateful for the consideration of the bill.

chapters.summary: Brewer thanks Morano and turns the proceedings over to the committee clerk, William Martin, to call the roll on Proposed Introduction 320A.
chapters.title: Brewer turns to clerk to begin roll call vote

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I'll now turn it over to the clerk, who will soon, there he is, to call the roll.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Clerk William Martin calls the roll. Brewer, Dinowitz, Feliz, Stevens, Zhuang, Wilson, and Morano all vote aye, with several offering congratulations to Morano and Staten Island. Dinowitz notes Staten Island joins the Bronx and Brooklyn with a codified flag.
chapters.title: Roll call vote: all committee members vote aye on Intro 320A

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Good morning, William Martin, Committee Clerk, Committee on Governmental Operations, State and Federal Legislation, Proposed Introduction 320A, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Brewers.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Dinowitz.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: Congratulations, Councilman Murano.

utterances.speaker: Eric Dinowitz
utterances.text: The entire island of Staten for joining the ranks of the Bronx and Brooklyn who have flags.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Feliz.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: I vote aye or no.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Congratulations, Councilman Morano, and also to the people of Staten Island.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Let's go Bronx.

utterances.speaker: Oswald J. Feliz
utterances.text: Let's go Yankees.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Zhuang.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Thank you, Councilmember Stevens.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Zhuang.

utterances.speaker: Susan Zhuang
utterances.text: I vote aye and a congratulation to our council member, Monrado, and also Southern Island people.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Wilson.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: I vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Congratulations, Manhattan.

utterances.speaker: Carl Wilson
utterances.text: Tips its hat to Staten Island today.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Morano.

utterances.speaker: Frank Morano
utterances.text: Enthusiastically, yes.

chapters.summary: The clerk announces the bill passed by a vote of seven in the affirmative, zero in the negative, with no abstentions—a full committee vote. Chair Brewer declares the hearing finished.
chapters.title: Bill approved 7-0 by committee; hearing adjourned

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: By a vote of seven in the affirmative, zero in the negative, and no abstentions.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Item has been approved by the committee.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Madam Chair, that is a full committee.

utterances.speaker: Council Staff
utterances.text: Chair Brewer.

utterances.speaker: Gale A. Brewer
utterances.text: Hearing is finished.

summary: The Committee on Governmental Operations, State & Federal Legislation held a hearing on Intro 320A, a bill to codify the official flag of the borough of Staten Island.
Chair Gale Brewer and Council Member Frank Morano explained the flag's history, design symbolism, and significance for Staten Island civic identity.
The committee voted 7-0 to approve the bill, with bipartisan support from the entire Staten Island delegation.
title: Committee on Governmental Operations, State & Federal Legislation
topic: Codifying the official flag of the borough of Staten Island
